claim_1.claim: Flow Cytometry Tsurf v1 analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients and healthy controls showed marked reductions in T cell number and frequency in both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells

sources.quote: We analysed PBMC and plasma samples from patients with moderate or severe COVID-19 and healthy HCW donors by flow cytometry and ELISA to quantify leukocytes and soluble mediators, respectively.
COVID-19 patients presented with marked reductions in T cell number and frequency in both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, even after normalization for age as a possible confounder.

comparison.finding: marked reductions in T cell number and frequency in moderate COVID-19 vs healthy
marked reductions in T cell number and frequency in severe COVID-19 vs healthy

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry Myeloid CD11c analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients shows increases in monocytes, low-density neutrophils, and eosinophils correlating with disease severity.

sources.quote: In patients with COVID-19, increases in monocytes, low-density neutrophils and eosinophils correlated with the severity of disease.

comparison.finding: increases in monocytes, low-density neutrophils, and eosinophils in severe vs moderate COVID-19

claim_3.claim: Cytokine array analysis of plasma from healthy and COVID -19 patients showed that CRS-linked cytokines such as IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, IL-18, TNF showed stronger positive associations in patients with severe COVID-19.

sources.quote: Most of the cytokines linked to cytokine release syndrome (CRS), such as IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, IL-18 and TNF, showed increased positive associations in patients with severe disease (Fig. 1d–f, Extended Data Fig. 3).

comparison.finding: CRS-linked cytokines showed increased positive associations/correlations in patients with severe COVID-19.

claim_4.claim: Cytokine array analysis of plasma from COVID-19 patients showed that after an early increase in cytokines, patients with moderate COVID-19 displayed progressive reduction in type 1 inflammatory markers including IFNα2, IFNγ, IL-12p70, CXCL9, and CXCL10, and type 3 inflammatory markers including IL-17A, IL-22, and IL-23, whereas patients with severe COVID-19 maintained elevated responses throughout disease progression.

sources.quote: Following an early increase in cytokines, patients with moderate COVID-19 displayed a progressive reduction in type 1 (antiviral) and type 3 (antifungal) responses. By contrast, patients with severe COVID-19 maintained these elevated responses throughout the course of the disease.
Fig. 2a shows longitudinal cytokine measurements including IFNα2, IFNγ, IL-12p70, CXCL9, CXCL10, IL-17A, IL-22, and IL-23.

comparison.finding: After early cytokine elevation, moderate COVID-19 patients showed progressive reduction in type 1 markers IFNα2, IFNγ, IL-12p70, CXCL9, and CXCL10, and type 3 markers IL-17A, IL-22, and IL-23, whereas severe COVID-19 patients maintained elevated responses over the disease course.

claim_5.claim: Real time polymerase chain reaction assay of nasopharyngeal swabs from COVID-19 patients showed no significant difference in viral RNA load between moderate and severe disease at specific time points, but a steady decline in viral load over the course of disease in moderate patients, unlike in severe patients.

sources.quote: We assessed viral RNA load (quantified by quantitative PCR with reverse transcription (RT–qPCR) using nasopharyngeal swabs).

Although there was no significant difference in viral RNA load between patients with moderate and severe disease at any specific time point analysed, patients with moderate disease showed a steady decline in viral load over the course of disease, whereas those with severe disease did not.

comparison.finding: no significant difference in viral RNA load between moderate and severe at specific time points
